retained_original_metadata.title: Coherent-sheaf dg categories of blowups with the transformed divisor deleted are the stated homotopy pushouts for a smooth codimension-two center in a divisor
retained_original_metadata.author: Benjamin Gammage; Ian Le
retained_original_metadata.source_title: Mirror Symmetry for Truncated Cluster Varieties
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs two geometric functors from the center and ambient variety and identifies their restrictions only after deleting the transformed divisor. It then uses the blowup semiorthogonal decomposition to prove essential surjectivity and identifies the quotient by divisor-supported objects with the claimed homotopy coequalizer. The new geometric localization-to-pushout comparison is substantially more than applying the prior blowup decomposition alone.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Complete author Theorem4.13 statement, diagram and proof are supplied: X is a smooth variety or DM stack, D is its specified divisor and H is smooth of codimension2 in X contained in D. The open space is Bl_H(X) with the strict transform of D deleted; the homotopy diagram uses derived i-star from Coh(D) to Coh(H) and k-pushforward to Coh(X). All dg and coherent-category conventions are retained. The author constructs FH=j-star i-pushforward q-star and FX=j-star p-star, explains their agreement after restriction, and gives the full semiorthogonal-generation/localization argument. Orlov blowup decomposition and divisor localization are genuinely prior background, not claimed as newly proved here. This independent geometric pushout theorem is selected, rather than the HMS theorem4.12 or a helper variant. The official revised-version notice on physical page1 concerning removal of an erroneous old Section5 is preserved; the selected current theorem lies in the retained Section4 and does not use that removed section.
